summary: @servicetitan/temporal-lite preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall hook (package.json scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs") runs setup.mjs, which downloads a Bun JavaScript runtime from oven-sh's GitHub releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB heavily-obfuscated bundle using shuffled string-array indirection (array-rotation decoder, hex-named identifiers, integer-index string table over a scrambled alphabet) whose behavior is hidden from static review. Fetching an alternate JavaScript runtime and executing a large obfuscated payload through it on `npm install` is inconsistent with the package's advertised purpose (a Temporal date/time polyfill) and matches an alternate-runtime dropper pattern designed to evade Node-based scanners. The package name uses the @servicetitan scope and the repository URL points to github.com/servicetitan/anvil-uikit-contrib.git, presenting the package as first-party ServiceTitan tooling, while the package.json description and author metadata are empty.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
